## Done — streaming Protocol Buffers wire-format codec

Implemented the full codec in MoonBit in eight focused root-package files, plus a comprehensive README and specification-derived tests.

### Implementation
| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `readers.mbt` | `BytesReader`, `LimitedReader` (opaque, `priv` fields), `read_exact_fixed` / `read_exact_bytes` / `skip_exact` looping over partial reads |
| `varint.mbt` | Base-128 varint reader (10-byte limit, bits past the 64th dropped, 11th-byte overflow), zigzag encode/decode 32/64 |
| `keys.mbt` | `read_tag` (`(field << 3) | wire`, rejects field 0 and wire types 6/7) and `write_tag` |
| `scalars.mbt` | int32/int64/uint32/uint64/sint32/sint64/bool/enum readers, hand-assembled little-endian fixed32/64, bit-exact float/double |
| `records.mbt` | int32-bounded length prefixes, `bytes`, `read_packed` through a `LimitedReader`, `read_unknown` with an iterative group stack (mismatched/unbalanced groups rejected) |
| `utf8.mbt` | strict UTF-8 validation via `@utf8.decode` (BOM preserved), `write_string` rejecting unpaired surrogates |
| `encode.mbt` | canonical minimal writers for every scalar kind |
| `errors.mbt` | `Truncated` / `Malformed` suberror |

Streaming correctness: varints are read one byte at a time (no pushback available), fixed-width/length-delimited values gather exactly what they need across calls, and EOF inside any value raises. Payloads are assembled in 4 KiB chunks so a `2^31-1` length prefix cannot trigger a huge allocation before truncation is detected.

## Key implementation decisions

- **Streaming:** `read_exact_into` loops until a value is complete (short reads are normal), rejects a zero-length "success", and raises `Truncated` at EOF inside a value; `LimitedReader` confines reads to a window.
- **Varints:** any ≤10-byte encoding accepted (non-minimal included), bits past the 64th dropped, an 11th continuation byte raises `Overflow`; the 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits; writers emit minimal form; negative `int32`/`enum` are sign-extended to ten bytes; zigzag computed on bit patterns so extremes are exact.
- **Keys/unknown fields:** field number 0 and wire types 6/7 raise; `read_unknown` skips varint/8/4/LEN records and whole nested groups, rejecting mismatched or unopened end tags.
- **Length-delimited:** the 2^31−1 bound is checked on the whole 64-bit varint (so 2^32 is rejected), and payloads are accumulated in ≤512-byte chunks so a hostile length cannot force a huge allocation (this is what makes "arbitrary bytes never panic" hold).
- **Packed:** decoded through a `LimitedReader`, with a progress guard replacing a possible infinite loop.
- **UTF-8:** overlong forms, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncated sequences and stray continuation bytes rejected; NUL, C1 controls and a leading U+FEFF preserved.

## Key behaviors

- **Grammar-driven (whitelist) validation per component**, so spaces, `<>`, `\`, `^`, backtick, `{}`, `|`, `"`, control and non-ASCII characters are rejected everywhere without being listed; every `%` must start a complete `XXXX` triplet.
- **IPv6** validated by splitting at the single `::` (8 groups without it, ≤ 7 with it, embedded IPv4 counts as the `ls32` pair, IPv4 only as the final segment); brackets are kept in `host`, zone IDs keep their `%25` spelling.
- **`None` vs `Some("")`** preserved end-to-end: `http://h/p?` → `query = Some("")`, `http://h:/` → `port = Some("")`, `file:///x` → `host = Some("")`; `host: Some(_)` is the single authority flag.
- **Strict resolution** (`http:g` stays `http:g`), dot segments removed only from reference paths, never from an inherited base path.
- Only normalization is lowercasing the scheme; nothing is percent-decoded.
